subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw expose a single opt-in core TUI plain-text accessibility mode, and if so should its contract be `tui.accessibility.plainText` with ASCII replacements rather than a narrower emoji-only toggle?
rationale: This is a new persisted configuration and user-visible presentation contract; source confirms that neither the configuration shape nor validation currently defines it, and the issue's requested behavior spans both OpenClaw-owned rendering and a framework-owned selection glyph.

options.title: Sponsor one TUI plain-text mode
options.body: Add an opt-in `tui.accessibility.plainText` contract with documented ASCII replacements and supported handling for the pi-tui selection indicator.

options.title: Defer the config surface
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until maintainers choose whether broader TUI accessibility settings belong in the core product.

options.title: Narrow to targeted accessibility fixes
options.body: Address confirmed high-noise render paths without adding a broad setting, accepting that users cannot opt out of all decorative Unicode consistently.

recommendation.title: Sponsor one TUI plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in `tui.accessibility.plainText` contract with documented ASCII replacements and supported handling for the pi-tui selection indicator.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature and configuration history most directly connect this person to the core TUI and config boundary involved in the product decision.
